reading.body:
Ed Pagano is named on 56 AI lobbying filings, and the clients on those filings are mostly software companies rather than power or data center developers.

The client list runs from Salesforce and OpenAI at the top down through Dropbox, Microsoft, Adobe, Amazon and SAP. That is a software and cloud roster. The one exception is STACK Infrastructure, named on 5 filings, which builds data centers. So the AI lobbying recorded here is concentrated on the application and platform layer, with a single infrastructure builder present at the bottom of the list.

Two bills appear, S 3982 and HR 7786, both tied to filings from 2025 or later. The data does not say what either bill would do, so it cannot support any claim about whether the lobbying concerned permitting, disclosure, procurement or something else. The prior government positions are disclosed under the Lobbying Disclosure Act and are identical across four filings: Senate staff and executive branch roles ending in 2014. That establishes a revolving door pattern but says nothing about which positions connect to which client.

What this does not cover is money. No filing amounts, no spending totals, no agencies contacted, and no indication of how many of the 56 filings are amendments or duplicates. The count of 56 is a count of filings naming him, not a measure of influence. The page also notes a different lobbyist shares the name, so any figure read here should be tied to LDA lobbyist id 71754.

summary: Ed Pagano is named as a lobbyist on 56 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 71754. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
